title: Generic and Maintenance Generic Copays on a Prescription Insurance on File Corrected Claim
content:
**Prescription Insurance on File** sets the copay of a corrected claim by the product dispensed on the corrected fill and the patient's generic refill history for the same prescription, as the fill ledger under Prescriptions shows them.

## Rule

- When the corrected fill is a **generic** and at least **3** generic refills of the same prescription settled through insurance were dispensed less than **3** whole months before the day the corrected claim is made, the maintenance generic copay of **10.00** applies.
- When the corrected fill is a generic and fewer such refills were dispensed, the generic copay of **15.00** applies.
- Otherwise — a corrected fill that is not a generic — the plan's standard copay of **25.00** applies.

## Terms, as the records show them

- **Generic** — the product dispensed on the refill is recorded as generic.
- **Settled through insurance** — the refill's payment basis is insurance; a refill paid in cash is not counted.
- **Same prescription** — refills of the prescription the corrected fill belongs to; refills of other prescriptions are not counted. The corrected fill itself counts when it meets these terms.

## Condition table

| Corrected fill's product | Generic refills of the same prescription, settled through insurance, dispensed less than 3 whole months before | Copay |
|---|---|---|
| Generic | 3 or more | 10.00 |
| Generic | 0, 1 or 2 | 15.00 |
| Brand | any number | 25.00 (standard copay) |

## Illustrations (hypothetical, corrected claim made on 10 June)

- Generic refills settled through insurance on 12 March, 12 April and 12 May, the corrected fill being the 12 May refill: 3 refills, all less than 3 whole months before 10 June — 10.00.
- The same, but the first refill was dispensed on 10 March: exactly 3 whole months before, so it is not counted; 2 refills — 15.00.
- Three generic refills in the window, one of them paid in cash: 2 counted — 15.00.
